sources.title: Martin Fowler — The Practical Test Pyramid
supports: Minimal E2E high-value journeys and lower-level integration coverage

sources.title: Playwright — Best Practices
supports: User-visible assertions and isolated E2E testing, avoiding implementation details
notes: Test user-visible behavior; Make tests as isolated as possible; Use locators

sources.title: Playwright — Authentication
supports: Isolated browser state and separate test users for mutating flows
notes: Introduction; Moderate: one account per parallel worker

sources.title: UK Home Office — Test Pyramid
supports: Limit E2E to critical journeys while automating more unit and integration tests
notes: Must avoid large numbers of end-to-end tests

claims.statement: E2E suites should concentrate on a very small number of the application's most valuable complete user journeys, leaving edge cases to lower layers.
claims.rationale: Fowler recommends keeping E2E sparse, and proving boundary conditions at lower levels.

claims.statement: Browser tests should assert user-visible outcomes and avoid private implementation details.
claims.rationale: Official Playwright guide defines robust user-facing assertions.

claims.statement: Browser state should be isolated between tests; tests that mutate shared server state may need separate test accounts.
claims.locator: Introduction; Moderate: one account per parallel worker
claims.rationale: Playwright authentication documentation details isolation and per-worker accounts.

claims.statement: A test pyramid favors many cheap unit tests, fewer integration tests and a limited set of E2E scenarios for critical flows.
claims.locator: Requirements; You MUST avoid large numbers of end-to-end tests
claims.rationale: Government engineering guidance describes stage selection based on risk and maintenance cost.
